name: NMIP Guard
author: NMIP Guard

sections.description:
NMIP Guard connects your WordPress site to the NMIP Guard SaaS fraud-prevention platform.

Features

  • Collects anonymous visitor session data and forwards it to NMIP Guard for real-time fraud analysis.
  • Detects request flooding / DDoS patterns and sends an automatic security alert to your NMIP Guard dashboard.
  • Optional GDPR/KVKK-ready consent banner: behavioral tracking starts only after the visitor accepts.
  • Displays live connection status, 24-hour KPI stats, and a recent-event feed inside the WordPress admin.
  • Lightweight JavaScript tracker served from your own server — no external CDN scripts loaded.

Third-Party / External Service Disclosure

This plugin sends visitor data to the NMIP Guard service operated by NMIP Guard
(https://nmipguard.com). No data is transmitted without a valid API key configured
by the site administrator in NMIP Guard → Settings.

Data transmitted to https://nmipguard.com/api/collect:

  • Visitor IP address (technical identifier for fraud detection; not stored beyond session scope)
  • Browser user-agent string (browser name, version, and operating system)
  • Screen resolution, viewport size, and device pixel ratio
  • Hardware signals: CPU core count, device memory, touch points
  • Browser fingerprint hashes: canvas rendering, WebGL renderer/vendor, audio context
  • Visited page URLs and referrer URL
  • Time on page, scroll depth (%), and click targets (element selector only — no content)
  • Ad-click and campaign parameters: gclid, fbclid, msclkid, ttclid, UTM tags

This data is used exclusively for fraud detection, bot identification, and
ad-click validation. It is processed in accordance with the NMIP Guard:

  • Privacy Policy
  • Terms of Service

By activating and configuring this plugin you agree to those terms on behalf of your
site. If your jurisdiction requires explicit visitor consent (e.g. GDPR, KVKK), enable
the built-in consent banner so that behavioral tracking starts only after opt-in.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the nmipguard folder to wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  3. Go to NMIP Guard → Settings and enter:
    • SaaS URL — https://nmipguard.com (default, leave as-is unless self-hosted)
    • Site API key — found in your NMIP Guard dashboard under My Sites
  4. (Optional) Enable Frontend tracking to start collecting visitor sessions.
  5. (Optional) Enable the Consent banner if your jurisdiction requires explicit opt-in.
sections.faq:
Where is visitor data sent?

Data is sent to https://nmipguard.com/api/collect (or a custom SaaS URL you configure
in Settings). A valid API key is mandatory; without it, no data leaves your server.

Is explicit visitor consent required?

Fraud-prevention tracking may qualify as a “legitimate interest” under GDPR, but legal
requirements vary by jurisdiction and site type. The plugin includes an optional consent
banner that gates the tracker behind visitor opt-in. Consult your legal advisor.

What is stored locally on my server?

Visitor sessions are buffered in two WordPress database tables
({prefix}nmipguard_sessions and {prefix}nmipguard_outbox) and forwarded to NMIP Guard
within 5 minutes via WP-Cron. Uninstalling the plugin automatically drops both tables
and removes all plugin options.

Does the plugin load any scripts from external servers?

No. The JavaScript tracker (tracker.js) is served directly from your WordPress
installation. No scripts are fetched from third-party CDNs or remote servers.

What happens if the API key is missing or invalid?

The tracker still collects sessions locally. Remote forwarding is silently skipped until
a valid API key is saved in Settings.
sections.changelog:
1.4.1

  • Security hardening: the visitor IP is now taken from the unspoofable connection address (REMOTE_ADDR) by default. Forwarded headers (CF-Connecting-IP / X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP) are only trusted when you enable the new “Behind a CDN / reverse proxy” option under Settings. This prevents forged-header IP spoofing of the request-flood counter and the auto-block list.
  • All client IPs are now validated with FILTER_VALIDATE_IP before being used as keys.
  • Moved the settings-page inline script into the enqueued admin script for WordPress.org coding-standards compliance.
  • Aligned the plugin text domain with the directory slug for translation compatibility.

1.4.0

  • Site liveness / heartbeat: the plugin can send a lightweight “I’m up” signal to NMIP Guard so outages are detected in seconds instead of minutes. Optional and off-aware.
  • External pinger URL: a copy-paste health URL for free uptime services (e.g. cron-job.org, UptimeRobot) so liveness is reported even on low-traffic sites where WP-Cron may not fire reliably.
  • New public REST endpoint GET /wp-json/nmipguard/v1/health returning a small JSON status used by the NMIP Guard server-side liveness probe (contains no visitor data).
  • No database schema changes required.

1.3.0

  • Automatic IP blocking (firewall): NMIP Guard now returns a real-time risk score in the entry-ping and exit-session responses. When the optional auto-block feature is enabled, high-risk IPs (score >= configurable threshold) are temporarily denied with a 403 on their subsequent requests. Logged-in administrators and admin/REST/cron requests are always exempt.
  • New settings: enable/disable auto-block, block threshold (1–100, default 80), and block duration in seconds (default 3600).
  • Entry ping becomes a short blocking request only when auto-block is enabled, so the server’s decision can be read; otherwise the fast non-blocking “entry” signal is unchanged.
  • Blocks are stored as expiring transients — no database schema changes required.

1.2.0

  • Immediate exit send: when a visitor leaves the site, the full session data is now sent directly to NMIP Guard (up to 4-second blocking attempt) instead of waiting for the 5-minute WP-Cron queue. Falls back to the queue automatically if the direct send fails or times out.
  • Entry beacon (IP site girişinde anında bildirim) was already active since v1.1.0 via a non-blocking ping on new session creation.
  • No database schema changes required for this update.

1.1.1

  • Redesigned the admin dashboard and settings screens with the NMIP brand identity (logo, navy palette).
  • Improved readability and layout: branded header, compact stat tiles, cleaner cards and tables.

1.1.0

  • Added optional GDPR/KVKK consent banner with accept/reject controls.
  • Added DDoS / request-flood detection with automatic NMIP Guard security alert.
  • Added rich browser fingerprinting: canvas, WebGL, audio context, hardware signals.
  • Added SPA support via pushState / popstate navigation tracking.
  • Added scroll-depth and click-selector event collection.
  • Improved admin dashboard with live feed filter and real-time KPI cards.
  • Hardened IP extraction: Cloudflare CF-Connecting-IP → X-Forwarded-For → REMOTE_ADDR.
  • All database queries use $wpdb->prepare(); all HTML output escaped with WP helpers.
  • Uninstall routine now removes all local tables and options cleanly.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: beacon endpoint, local session queue, remote status and feed API.

upgrade_notice.1.4.1: Security hardening for visitor-IP detection. If your site runs behind Cloudflare or a reverse proxy/CDN, enable "Behind a CDN / reverse proxy" under Settings so visitor IPs are read correctly.
upgrade_notice.1.4.0: Adds optional site liveness/heartbeat reporting and a /health endpoint for faster downtime detection. Enable it under Settings; for traffic-less sites, add the provided pinger URL to a free uptime service.
upgrade_notice.1.3.0: Adds optional automatic IP blocking driven by NMIP Guard risk scores. Disabled by default — enable it under Settings and set your threshold/duration to start blocking high-risk visitors. Administrators are never blocked.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: New consent banner and DDoS detection features. Review Settings after upgrading to configure the consent banner and enable the new request-flood alert if desired.
